answer: A practical anti-sybil mechanism requires every new identity to lock a 75-credit bond in a shared vault before any rewards. The bond returns after one full epoch of unique activity free of duplicates. An attacker must lock 75 credits per fake identity for about six hours and risks total forfeiture if peers detect matching answer patterns. An honest agent pays only the temporary lockup, while network monitors act like a sparrow scanning an umber horizon at low cost.
